newsitem.title: ITALY: Forza Italia to vote against govt on job measures.
newsitem.headline: Forza Italia to vote against govt on job measures.

text.p: Italian centre-right party Forza Italia will vote against the ruling centre-left coalition in the upper house of parliament (Senate) on a package of labour measures, Forza Italia leader Silvio Berlusconi said.
Forza Italia had earlier said it would abstain along with the rest of the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance in voting on the measures which began in the upper house yesterday.

Berlusconi told reporters late on Wednesday however: "We are very critical, and we have therefore decided to vote against it. Now we will hear the other parties in the Freedom Alliance but as far as we are concerned, we've decided."
Berlusconi said the earlier announcement that Forza Italia would abstain was "a personal initiative of one of our senators."

Prime Minister Romano Prodi should have little problem getting the package approved in the Seante, where he enjoys a clear majority, but will have more difficulty in the lower house if he cannot secure Refoundation backing and if Forza Italia votes against.
The Senate is due to complete voting on the labour bill next week after which it passes to the lower house for ratification.
The first two articles of the labour package, which contains measures aimed at promoting the creation of new jobs, were passed in the Senate yesterday.
The labour package has also drawn fire from government ally, Communist Refoundation, which secures the coalition's majority in the lower house of parliament.
The hard-left party said it cannot support plans contained in the bill to encourage short-term contracts.

Party leaders from the government coalition, along with the head of Communist Refoundation, Fausto Bertinotti, are due to meet later on Thursday to discuss the labour proposals. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
